name: Cell Passaging
description: Routine subculture (passaging) of adherent mammalian cells using trypsin-EDTA. Keep cells in logarithmic growth phase. Typical split ratio: 1:3 to 1:10 depending on cell line.
source_note: General educational template for routine adherent mammalian cell passaging.

steps.title: Pre-warm media and reagents
steps.description: Pre-warm complete cell culture medium, PBS, and trypsin-EDTA to 37°C in a water bath. Cold reagents can cause cell damage and shock.

reagents.name: Complete cell culture medium (e.g., DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% Pen-Strep)

steps.notes: Never microwave media or PBS — this may cause uneven heating and denature growth factors.

steps.title: Inspect cells and check confluency
steps.description: Observe cells under inverted microscope. Check confluency (typically passage at 70–90%), morphology, and signs of contamination (cloudiness, unusual morphology, color change in media).
steps.notes: Document passage number and confluency. Do not passage below 70% or above 95% — may select for abnormal cells.
steps.warnings: If contamination is suspected, do not proceed. Isolate flask immediately.

steps.title: Remove old media
steps.description: Transfer flask to laminar flow hood. Aspirate old medium from flask. Tilt flask slightly to remove as much media as possible.
steps.warnings: Discard media into appropriate biological waste container.

steps.title: Wash with PBS
steps.description: Add PBS to the flask, rinse the monolayer gently (tilt), and aspirate. Repeat once. This removes residual serum (which inhibits trypsin).
steps.notes: Two washes recommended for sensitive cell lines. Pour PBS gently down the side to avoid detaching cells.

steps.title: Add trypsin-EDTA and incubate
steps.description: Add a minimal volume of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA (enough to cover the cell monolayer). Incubate in the 37°C incubator for 3–7 min. Observe under microscope — cells should round up and detach.
steps.notes: Do not over-trypsinize — prolonged trypsin exposure damages cells. Tap flask gently to dislodge cells. Trypsin times vary: HeLa ~2 min, HEK293 ~3 min, fibroblasts ~5–10 min.
steps.warnings: Over-trypsinization damages cell surface proteins and reduces viability.

steps.title: Neutralize trypsin and collect cells
steps.description: Add 4–5× volume of complete medium (with serum) to neutralize trypsin. Pipette up and down several times to create a single-cell suspension and detach remaining cells.

steps.title: Centrifuge cell suspension
steps.description: Centrifuge the cell suspension to pellet cells and remove trypsin-containing media.
steps.notes: Avoid high speed — can damage cells. Cell pellet should be visible at bottom of tube.

steps.title: Resuspend and count cells
steps.description: Aspirate supernatant completely. Resuspend cell pellet in fresh complete medium by gentle pipetting. Take an aliquot for cell counting using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter with trypan blue.
steps.notes: Viability > 90% expected for healthy cells. Record cell count and viability.
steps.warnings: Trypan blue is a potential carcinogen — handle with care.

steps.title: Seed cells into new flask
steps.description: Calculate volume needed for desired seeding density. Add fresh complete medium to new flask(s). Add appropriate volume of cell suspension. Homogenize by gentle rocking.
equipment: New cell culture flask(s) (T-25 or T-75)
steps.notes: Typical seeding density: 5,000–20,000 cells/cm² depending on cell line. Label flask with cell line, passage number, date, and your initials.

steps.title: Return to incubator
steps.description: Place flasks flat in 37°C, 5% CO₂ humidified incubator. Check next day to confirm cell attachment and normal morphology.
steps.notes: Check cells after 24 h for attachment. Do not disturb for 12–24 h after seeding.
